text: A model that defines active member correctly today only matters if it stays correct every night. This video adds the tests that make that a guarantee instead of a hope.

Generic dbt tests catch structural problems any table can have. A dbt_utils grain test confirms last lesson's dedupe actually worked. Neither of those catches Brightleaf's specific business rule -- that takes a custom test.

This singular test self-joins the membership history looking for one membership claiming two different statuses on the same day. If it ever returns a row, the active-member definition can't be trusted until the source is fixed.
Tests get named clearly on purpose -- a failure should tell whoever's on call exactly what broke, not just that something did.
The business rule is now enforced automatically, every run. Next: turning this logic into the two tables every team will actually query.
